slides.0.title: Coastal Region I: Stellenbosch
slides.0.subtitle: Mountain wards and Cabernet
slides.1.title: History and terroir
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Founded in 1679
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Simon van der Stel founded Stellenbosch in 1679, South Africa's second-oldest European settlement after Cape Town
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Sources of cooling
slides.1.highlights.1.content: False Bay about 20 km to the south, the Benguela Current and the summer-afternoon Cape Doctor
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Soils
slides.1.highlights.2.content: More than 50 soil types: decomposed granite on mountain slopes, Table Mountain Sandstone on higher ridges, alluvial loam over clay subsoils on valley floors
slides.1.content: Stellenbosch's hallmark is diversity of mountains, sea and soils: temperature and rainfall vary widely within the district.
slides.2.title: Wards and varieties
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Eight official wards
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Banghoek, Bottelary, Devon Valley, Jonkershoek Valley, Papegaaiberg, Polkadraai Hills, Simonsberg-Stellenbosch and Vlottenburg; Helderberg is a widely used informal sub-area
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Flagship variety
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Cabernet Sauvignon is the flagship; Bordeaux-style blends, Chenin Blanc and Pinotage are also important, with Syrah, Sauvignon Blanc and Chardonnay common
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Source discrepancies
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Planted area differs widely between sources (about 11,500 to 17,500 ha), so no area question is set
slides.2.content: Anchor your memory on Cabernet and the mountain wards; check official sources for detailed figures.
